# AIDE — Autonomous Intent-Driven Engineering

> The canonical home of the AIDE methodology and the @aidemd-mcp/server package — a short `.aide` intent spec lives next to the code it governs, and that spec is the contract every agent plans, builds, and QAs against.

AIDE (Autonomous Intent-Driven Engineering) treats intent as a first-class artifact. A short `.aide` doc sits next to each orchestrator, declares the module's scope, intent, and outcomes, and becomes the contract downstream agents work from. `@aidemd-mcp/server` is the MCP server that ships AIDE as a set of commands, subagents, and skills a Claude Code (or compatible) host can install in one step.

If you are an agent operating inside a codebase that ships `.aide` files, this methodology governs how you read those specs, plan from them, build against them, and validate your output. The docs below are the authoritative reference for every stage of that pipeline.

To install the methodology into a host project, run `npx @aidemd-mcp/server init`. To browse the docs in a human-readable form, visit https://aidemd.dev/.

## Methodology

- [AIDE Methodology Doc Hub](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/index): AIDE ships the canonical pipeline agents that aide_init installs to .claude/agents/aide/.
- [AIDE Spec](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/aide-spec): Autonomous Intent-Driven Engineering (AIDE) puts intent at the center of everything.
- [AIDE Template](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/aide-template): For agents: this file is a scaffold, not a reference.
- [plan.aide Spec](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/plan-aide): The architect's implementation plan.
- [todo.aide Spec](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/todo-aide): The QA re-alignment document.
- [brief.aide Spec](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/brief-aide): The architect's pre-read.
- [session.aide Spec](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/session-aide): The session record.
- [brain.aide Spec](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/brain-aide): brain.aide is the host project's brain configuration.
- [Progressive Disclosure](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/progressive-disclosure): Code structured so understanding deepens on demand, not all at once.
- [Agent-Readable Code](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/agent-readable-code): The outcome of progressive disclosure.
- [Automated QA](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/automated-qa): The verification loop of AIDE.
- [Cascading Alignment](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/cascading-alignment): The AIDE intent tree is a hierarchy of .aide specs: root intent at the top, module specs below, submodule specs below those.
- [Changelog](https://aidemd.dev/docs/methodology/changelog): All notable changes to @aidemd-mcp/server are recorded here.

## Commands

- [/aide — Orchestrator](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide): /aide is a router.
- [/aide:align — Alignment Phase](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/align): Verify spec-vs-spec alignment and brevity across the intent tree.
- [/aide:brain — Brain Interface](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/brain): General-purpose interface to the project's brain, plus a config mode that creates, repairs and wires the brain config (or repoints it at a different location).
- [/aide:build — Build Phase](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/build): Execute the architect's implementation plan.
- [/aide:fix — Fix Phase](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/fix): Work one unchecked item from the todo.aide checklist.
- [/aide:handoff — Session Handoff](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/handoff): Invoke the aide-handoff skill via the Skill tool — that is your only valid response to /aide:handoff.
- [/aide:plan — Plan Phase](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/plan): Translate the intent spec into a step-by-step implementation plan.
- [/aide:qa — QA Phase](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/qa): Verify actual output against the intent spec.
- [/aide:refactor — Refactor Phase](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/refactor): Refactor existing artifacts to close drift from canonical contracts.
- [/aide:research — Research Phase (Optional)](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/research): Fill the brain with durable domain knowledge the synthesizer can later draw from.
- [/aide:spec — Spec Phase](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/spec): Produce the .aide intent spec frontmatter only.
- [/aide:synthesize — Synthesize Phase](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/synthesize): Read the intent spec's frontmatter, the orchestrator's description of the pipeline flow and any brain research, then fill in the .aide body sections (Context, Strategy, Good examples, Bad examples,…
- [/aide:update-playbook — Playbook Maintenance](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/update-playbook): Call aide_brain once.
- [/aide:upgrade — Interactive Methodology Upgrade](https://aidemd.dev/docs/commands/aide/upgrade): Bring this project's AIDE methodology artifacts up to date with canonical by calling aide_upgrade and walking the user through each drifted category interactively.

## Agents

- [aide-aligner](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-aligner): Use this agent when you need to verify that specs across the intent tree are internally consistent — comparing child outcomes against ancestor outcomes to detect intent drift. This agent walks the full ancestor chain, compares outcomes at each level, and produces todo.aide at any node where drift is found. It does NOT check code against specs (that is QA) and does NOT rewrite spec outcomes.
- [aide-architect](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-architect): Use this agent when a .aide spec is ready and needs to be translated into an implementation plan, or, in structure mode, before any spec below the project root is written, to propose the project folder tree for the user's approval (structure mode writes no file). In plan mode the agent reads the spec (frontmatter; body sections if present), reads brief.aide if present, consults the coding playbook, scans the codebase, and produces plan.aide with checkboxed steps. It does NOT write code or delegate to other agents.
- [aide-auditor](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-auditor): Use this agent when existing, working code needs to be reviewed for drift from coding playbook conventions. This agent reads the implementation, consults the coding playbook, and produces plan.aide with refactoring steps. It does NOT write code or delegate to other agents.
- [aide-domain-expert](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-domain-expert): Use this agent when the brain needs domain knowledge before the spec body can be filled. This agent does volume research — web, brain, external sources — and persists findings to the brain filed by domain, not by project. It does NOT fill the .aide spec or delegate to other agents.
- [aide-explorer](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-explorer): Use this agent for read-only investigation of the AIDE codebase — finding code, tracing bugs, answering questions about how modules work, or understanding the cascading intent tree. This agent understands the AIDE methodology, uses aide_discover for .aide file lookups, and navigates code using progressive disclosure. It does NOT write code, edit files, or delegate to other agents.
- [aide-implementor](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-implementor): Use this agent when you have plan.aide ready and need to execute it into working code (build mode), or when you need to fix exactly one todo.aide item (fix mode). This agent reads the plan, writes code, runs tests, and checks boxes. It does NOT make architectural decisions or delegate to other agents.
- [aide-maintainer](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-maintainer): Use this agent when a feature's pipeline phase has fully closed for a module — its plan.aide (if the module has one) has every step checked, any todo.aide is fully checked, and the retro (if QA wrote one) is promoted to brain — and the per-module ephemerals (brief.aide, plan.aide, todo.aide) need to be removed, leaving the code as the durable artifact. Verifies the retro promotion, records each file's closing status through `aide_frontmatter` (`completed`, or `abandoned` when the orchestrator says the user discarded the work), then removes the files through the `aide_cleanup` MCP tool, which enforces the status and checkbox preconditions in code and refuses with the exact open items. Never touches .aide/session.aide — it is never deleted. Does NOT create or update session.aide — that is the aide-spec-writer agent's job. Does NOT delete code, .aide intent specs, .aide/intent.aide, .aide/config/brain.aide, .aide/docs/, or any non-ephemeral file. Does NOT delegate to other agents.
- [aide-qa](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-qa): Use this agent when implementation is complete and needs to be verified against the .aide intent spec. This agent compares actual output against outcomes.desired and outcomes.undesired, then produces todo.aide with issues found. It does NOT propose solutions or delegate to other agents.
- [aide-spec-writer](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-spec-writer): Use this agent to write a structured AIDE file from orchestrator-supplied context. This agent handles TWO file types: (1) `.aide` intent spec frontmatter — the durable intent contract that drives every downstream pipeline phase (during /aide:spec). (2) `.aide/session.aide` — the project-wide pipeline-position log, which always exists: CREATE writes the empty placeholder when it is missing, and UPDATE writes whatever the orchestrator supplies, from the first piece of work on, whenever anything changes what it says (stage complete, paused for review, architectural decision settled, anti-regression invariant added). It never refuses for missing content and never needs a task to write. This agent does NOT interview the user — the orchestrator owns the user conversation and passes context via the delegation prompt; this agent formats that context into the canonical file type. Does NOT fill .aide body sections (that's the strategist), does NOT write code, does NOT delegate to other agents.
- [aide-strategist](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-strategist): Use this agent when the .aide frontmatter is complete and the feature is a pipeline — several modules handing off to each other in a specific order. This agent writes how the modules interact, from the orchestrator's description of the flow plus any brain research, into the spec's body sections (Context, Strategy, Good/Bad examples, References) AND authors the sibling brief.aide carrying the implementation contracts kicked out of the spec by the Brevity Contract. It reads from the brain, not the web. It does NOT delegate to other agents.
- [aide-upgrader](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/aide/aide-upgrader): Use this agent at the end of every /aide:upgrade to bring the project's own AIDE files up to the current format. It reads the `[migration]` entries in `.aide/docs/changelog.md`, finds every file still on an older form, and suggests the new value for each with the evidence behind it (REPORT). It then carries out exactly the changes the caller approved with the user, through the AIDE tools only, and verifies each one (APPLY). It never talks to the user, never decides a change itself, never touches files the changelog does not name, and never deletes anything. Does NOT delegate to other agents.
- [kanban-maintainer](https://aidemd.dev/docs/agents/kanban/kanban-maintainer): Use this agent for every read or write of the project's kanban tasks, so the tasks' full text never lands in the caller's context. Folders are the board: each project has its own folder with one subfolder per column. Reads: given a project tag and a query (open tasks, tasks by slug or search text, cleanup findings), it lists the project's column folders, reads each task and returns a compact report — per task its column, slug, priority, title, a short excerpt of what it is about, and its path. Writes: it carries out task changes the caller has ALREADY approved with the user (move, create, stash, complete, cleanup fixes) by following the kanban guides' task steps, verifies them, and returns exactly what changed. It never talks to the user, never decides which change to make, and never changes anything the caller did not name. Does NOT delegate to other agents.

## Skills

- [aide-brain-author — Write a Brain Config for Any Backend](https://aidemd.dev/docs/skills/aide-brain-author/skill): Author a brain config (`.aide/config/brain.aide`) for any brain backend, such as Jira, Notion, Confluence or a team wiki, one decision at a time with the user. It starts from the bundled template as a worked example, writes the launcher and every contract section for the user's backend from each section's published purpose, checks the draft's structure, then either swaps it in or leaves it beside the current config. It also adds missing contract sections to a config written for another backend. Invoke it when the user asks to create a brain config for a backend other than the bundled default, to rewrite their brain config for a different backend, or when `/aide:brain config` hands off a create or a custom-backend repair. Do NOT trigger for wiring, syncing, migrating or repairing a config that uses the bundled default backend; that stays with `/aide:brain config`.
- [/aide:handoff — Session Handoff](https://aidemd.dev/docs/skills/aide-handoff/skill): Record current pipeline state to `.aide/session.aide` — the project-wide pipeline-position log that lets the next session (yours or another agent's) resume from a known point. The file always exists, starting as an empty placeholder; every handoff is an UPDATE that writes whatever the agent has, with or without a task. `session.aide` is always kept up to date as the agent works. This skill is the orchestration layer: it gathers content from the invoking agent's conversation context and delegates the actual write to the `aide-spec-writer` agent in `session.aide` mode. Invoke this skill when the user types `/aide:handoff`, asks to "save the session" or "record where we are", and whenever anything changes what `session.aide` says — a stage starts or completes, a decision is settled, an invariant is added, a task moves, a release ships, or work outside the pipeline changes the state or the next step. Never end a turn or a session with `session.aide` behind. `session.aide` is never deleted — when a feature closes, UPDATE it for the next task.
- [aide-observer — the observer session](https://aidemd.dev/docs/skills/aide-observer/skill): Opens and keeps the observer session for an AIDE session: reports the session start and the user's request, starts the observer (one per user per machine), stops on a HALT when another session of the project is open or a BLOCKED when the observer cannot start, gives the user the link, and reports every pipeline action as it happens — pipelines, phases, skips, gates, plan steps, QA verdicts, files, commits. The observer is mandatory: it is the single source of truth for which session works in a project. Run this skill FIRST in every /aide session, before the `aide` skill, including when `aide` is invoked directly, unless the user said not to observe this session. Its reporting rules apply for the rest of the session.
- [/aide — Orchestrator](https://aidemd.dev/docs/skills/aide/skill): AIDE pipeline orchestrator — entry point for the conversational spec → research → synthesize → plan → build → QA → fix flow. Drives each phase by delegating to specialized subagents (aide-spec-writer, aide-architect, aide-implementor, aide-qa, etc.). Invoked when the user types /aide, asks to start an AIDE feature pipeline, asks to resume a pipeline already under way, or asks to align/refactor specs across the intent tree. **MANDATORY**: this skill begins with a non-skippable boot sequence — call `aide_info`, gate on brain status, read 6 methodology docs in parallel, run `aide_discover`, read `.aide/session.aide` (writing the empty placeholder if it is missing), then check the board through the `kanban` skill for open tasks. You MUST execute boot before reading or acting on the user's request, even when you think you have enough context. Skipping boot means orchestrating a methodology you don't know — you will guess at file formats, agent routing, and pipeline state, and produce drift.
- [brain — Signpost to the Brain](https://aidemd.dev/docs/skills/brain/skill): Signpost to the brain — an external, team-shareable knowledge store that holds context too durable for the repo and too cross-project for any single codebase (domain research, coding playbook, project history, journal, environment, identity, references). When the current task needs knowledge that isn't in the working directory, or the user references shared knowledge / research / conventions, invoke the `/aide:brain` slash command and let it discover and navigate the brain. This skill does NOT navigate the brain itself. Do NOT trigger for coding conventions or patterns (use `study-playbook` instead), for first-time brain wiring (that's `/aide:brain config`, which `/aide` routes to directly) or for writing a brain config for another backend (that's the `aide-brain-author` skill).
- [/kanban — Kanban Board](https://aidemd.dev/docs/skills/kanban/skill): Work the project's kanban board kept in the brain: create, work, manage, move, complete, stash and review tasks. Trigger when the user says "/kanban", "add a task", "create a task", "what should I work on", "move that task", "show the board", "stash context", "review the task", or otherwise asks to track, pick up, move or finish a piece of project work on the board.
- [/study-playbook — Load Coding Playbook Context](https://aidemd.dev/docs/skills/study-playbook/skill): Load relevant coding-playbook sections from the project's brain for the current task. Use this skill whenever you need to look up coding conventions, patterns, or architecture decisions before writing or reviewing code. Do NOT trigger for non-coding brain content.

## Tools

- [AIDE MCP tools](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/index): Every MCP tool the @aidemd-mcp/server package exposes, one page per tool.
- [aide_brain](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_brain): Read-only entry point to the brain config, returning one section of the host's config or the bundled template, the section contract, or a structural check of a draft config.
- [aide_cleanup](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_cleanup): Removes a closed module's pipeline files (plan.aide, todo.aide, brief.aide), refusing while any of them is still open.
- [aide_discover](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_discover): Maps where the project's .aide specs live, or gives one module's ancestor chain and subtree, so agents read intent before code.
- [aide_frontmatter](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_frontmatter): Reads or moves a governed frontmatter value, a spec's alignment or a plan, todo or brief's status, leaving every other byte of the file untouched.
- [aide_info](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_info): Boot-time report telling the orchestrator whether the server is behind, whether the project's AIDE files or hooks are out of date, and whether the brain is wired.
- [aide_init](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_init): Installs AIDE into a project one category at a time, writing new files itself and asking before anything is overwritten.
- [aide_inspect](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_inspect): Returns a code symbol's documentation, signature and kind without opening the whole source file.
- [aide_observer_end_session](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_observer_end_session): Ends another open session of the project after the user approves, so a HALT can be cleared.
- [aide_observer_event](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_observer_event): Reports one action of the session to the observer, recorded first in the session's own log outside the project and then shown live.
- [aide_observer_start](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_observer_start): Starts the observer, or reuses the running one, and halts the session if another session of the same project is open.
- [aide_read](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_read): Reads one .aide file and returns its content with its type, the other specs in its folder and the links it contains.
- [aide_scaffold](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_scaffold): Creates a blank AIDE working file under its canonical name, from intent specs to plans, todo lists and the session record, never over an existing file.
- [aide_upgrade](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_upgrade): Finds where the project's AIDE files have drifted from the version it runs and applies, one category at a time, only what the user confirms.
- [aide_validate](https://aidemd.dev/docs/tools/aide_validate): Health check for the spec layout, reporting orphaned or missing specs, plans with no spec, naming conflicts, broken links and frontmatter problems.

## Hooks

- [AIDE Claude Code hooks](https://aidemd.dev/docs/hooks/index): The five Claude Code hook events AIDE listens to, and what each one tells the observer about a session.
- [PostToolUse](https://aidemd.dev/docs/hooks/posttooluse): Fires after every tool call; AIDE records the session as working and links it to its observer session.
- [SessionEnd](https://aidemd.dev/docs/hooks/sessionend): Fires when a Claude Code session ends; AIDE records the session as ended and closes its observer session.
- [SessionStart](https://aidemd.dev/docs/hooks/sessionstart): Fires when a Claude Code session starts or resumes; AIDE records the session as working.
- [Stop](https://aidemd.dev/docs/hooks/stop): Fires when the agent finishes its turn; AIDE records the session as waiting on the user.
- [UserPromptSubmit](https://aidemd.dev/docs/hooks/userpromptsubmit): Fires when the user sends a message; AIDE records the session as working.
